the identification of a new Toc159-dependent import substrate in Arabidopsis.
the identification of an unusual Toc-dependent substrate and with the analysis of its import properties in the ppi1 and ppi2 mutants.
the unusual import behavior of RNP29.

the RNP29 protein precursor accumulates specifically in ppi2 protoplasts, but not in other ppi mutants, and that the N-terminal amino acids do not play an important role in the import process of this protein.
the RNP29 N-terminus is not essential for plastid import, but that it may play an important role in the regulation of the protein level in the plastid.

the RNP29 precursors are imported in a Toc159 dependent way but that the N-terminal amino acids have only minor effects on the import process and that the acetylation of the RNP 29 precursors is not related to their import.

the N-terminal methionine is not essential for the import of Toc159-dependent proteins into plastids but is a prerequisite for their efficient processing.

the RNP29 precursors accumulate in the ppi2 cytosol and that the N-terminal amino acids are not the only factor determining precursor accumulation in the ppi1/2 mutant.
